n94c96904591.s: Species diversity, the variety of species in an area, takes into account:
o: Only the number of species, irrespective of abundance
Only variation in genes within a single species
Only the variety of climatic zones
n94c96904591.x: Species diversity is the variety of species in an area and includes both richness and abundance.

n2abe6efa1b4.s: The total diversity across the ecosystems of a whole region is called:
n2abe6efa1b4.x: Gamma diversity is the regional total; beta diversity is species turnover between ecosystems and alpha is diversity within one area.

nb3027722c52.s: Which of the following is a recognised explanation for the greater biodiversity of tropical regions?
o: Long, undisturbed evolutionary history without glaciation
nb3027722c52.x: Tropical richness is linked to long evolutionary time without glaciation, a stable climate and more solar energy and productivity.

n23031f5c67b.s: A survey of ants found about how many species at the equator, against about 10 near the North Pole?
n23031f5c67b.x: The survey found about 10 ant species near the North Pole and up to about 2,000 at the equator, showing the latitudinal gradient.

n2cba7458d77.s: How many countries are recognised as the world's megadiverse countries?
n2cba7458d77.x: There are 17 megadiverse countries; 36 is the number of global biodiversity hotspots.

nf23f812e2f2.x: The hoolock gibbon of North-East India is India's only ape.

nc0b763e03fa.s: In 2025, India added how many animal species to its biodiversity records?
nc0b763e03fa.x: India added 709 animal species in 2025 (483 new to science and 226 new records), besides 353 plant taxa.

n6fa936a7178.s: The Trans-Himalaya biogeographic zone covers about what share of India's land?
n6fa936a7178.x: The Trans-Himalaya covers only about 5.7%; about 42% is the share of the Deccan Peninsula, the largest zone.

n6151bdb2415.s: The Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve in Andhra Pradesh was notified in:
n6151bdb2415.x: The Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve was notified in 2010; a sequence could not be built honestly from these facts.

n7056b5302bd.s: The Eastern Himalaya of India forms part of which biodiversity hotspot?
n7056b5302bd.x: The Eastern Himalaya belongs to the Himalaya hotspot; the Nicobar Islands belong to Sundaland.

nb6a35f17fb4.s: The National Biodiversity Authority, set up in 2003, is located at:
nb6a35f17fb4.x: The NBA was set up at Chennai in 2003; no dated sequence could be built honestly, so a one-liner is used.

n58d90975b1a.s:
Consider the following statements about the Biological Diversity (Amendment) Act, 2023:
1. It exempted AYUSH practitioners from prior intimation to State Biodiversity Boards.
2. It decriminalised offences and replaced them with penalties.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
n58d90975b1a.x: Both are provisions of the 2023 amendment.

n71794df9d47.s: Which of the following is excluded from the scope of Access and Benefit Sharing?
n71794df9d47.x: ABS covers plant, animal and microbial resources and traditional knowledge, but excludes human genetic material.

nc294da70706.s: The present, human-driven wave of extinctions is called the:
nc294da70706.x: The sixth mass extinction is the present human-driven wave; background extinction is slow natural loss at a low steady rate.

nce8d7a4445d.s: A species surviving only in captivity or cultivation, outside its natural range, is classed by IUCN as:
nce8d7a4445d.x: Extinct in the Wild denotes survival only in captivity or cultivation, outside the natural range; a ten-year gap alone does not make a species Extinct.

nf84b51a0c47.s: Which of the following is one of the defining tests for an invasive alien species in India?
nf84b51a0c47.x: The three tests are non-native origin, uncontrolled spread and measurable harm; commercial usefulness is not one.

n9ded56bbe07.s: The Directorate of Plant Protection, Quarantine and Storage (DPPQS) functions under the:
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
n9ded56bbe07.x: DPPQS functions under the Agriculture Ministry, not MoEFCC.

n442ecdb3962.s: Biodiversity loss reduces food security of resource-dependent communities mainly by disrupting:
o: Pollination, nutrient cycling and water and soil services
n442ecdb3962.x: Loss of pollination, nutrient cycling and water and soil services undermines food security.

n8fb66dbd7d4.s: The Phoenix Species Project (2026), with $200 million funding, aims to recover how many of the world's most threatened species?
n8fb66dbd7d4.x: The Re:wild and Bezos Earth Fund project aims to recover 100 of the most threatened species.

n2b6fa71e3cd.s: India's Red List Roadmap, led by the National Biodiversity Authority, aims to assess how many species by 2027?
n2b6fa71e3cd.x: The roadmap aims to assess 70,000 species by 2027.

new.s: Fuelwood, fodder and wild food used locally and not sold are examples of which value of biodiversity?
new.x: Consumptive value is local use without sale; productive value is commercial sale.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (value of biodiversity – example) is correctly matched?
new.x: Aesthetic value covers beauty and ecotourism; fuelwood is consumptive, sacred groves social and sold timber productive.

new.s: In India's 2025 biodiversity additions, which State recorded the highest number of new animal species?
new.x: Kerala led with 98, followed by West Bengal with 76.

new.s: Of the 709 animal species India added in 2025, how many were new to science?
new.x: 483 were new to science and 226 were new records for India.

new.s: India's 2025 species additions were compiled by:
new.x: The Botanical Survey of India and Zoological Survey of India released the 2025 additions.

new.s: The terms alpha, beta and gamma diversity were introduced by:
new.x: R.H. Whittaker introduced the terms alpha, beta and gamma diversity.

new.s: Among the world's countries, India ranks ____ in plant richness.
new.x: India is 10th in plant richness, 11th in endemic higher vertebrates and 6th as a centre of crop origin.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the 17 megadiverse countries?
new.x: Madagascar, Peru and Malaysia are in the list of 17 megadiverse countries; Thailand is not.

new.s: Over what share of India's animal species are endemic?
new.x: India holds about 7.5% of global fauna, and over 30% of its animals are endemic.

new.s: The estimate of 10–50 million total species on Earth is associated with:
new.x: Wilson (1992) estimated 10–50 million species; Robert May estimated about 7 million.

new.s: Robert May estimated the total number of species on Earth at about:
new.x: May estimated about 7 million; 1.5 million is the number described so far.

new.s: Plants make up about what share of recorded species?
new.x: Plants are about 22% of recorded species; animals are over 70%.

new.s: The Rivet popper hypothesis was proposed by:
new.x: Paul Ehrlich compared an ecosystem to an aeroplane and species to its rivets.

new.s: Under the Rodgers and Panwar scheme, India's biogeographic zones fall into how many biomes?
new.x: There are 2 realms, 5 biomes, 10 zones and 25 provinces.

new.s: Which biogeographic zone of India records the highest number of faunal species?
new.x: The Himalaya has the most faunal species (30,377); the Deccan Peninsula is the largest zone.

new.s: How many provinces does the Deccan Peninsula biogeographic zone have?
new.x: The Deccan Peninsula has 5 provinces, including Central Highlands, Chotanagpur and Deccan South.

new.s: The red panda occurs naturally in which part of India?
new.x: The red panda is found in the Eastern Himalaya: Sikkim, Arunachal and Darjeeling.

new.s: In India, the saltwater crocodile is found in:
new.x: The saltwater crocodile occurs in Bhitarkanika and the Sundarbans; Chambal is the gharial's home.

new.s: The Nilgiri tahr is naturally found only in the:
new.x: The Nilgiri tahr, like the lion-tailed macaque, is confined to the Western Ghats (Eravikulam).

new.s: In India, the Chinese pangolin is naturally found in:
new.x: The Chinese pangolin is found in the North-East; the Indian pangolin lives south of the Himalaya, not in the North-East.

new.s: The US patent on turmeric, challenged by CSIR, was revoked in:
new.x: The turmeric patent was revoked in 1997; the neem patent in 2000.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about biopiracy cases:
1. The neem patent held by W.R. Grace was revoked by the European Patent Office in 2000.
2. In the Basmati case, most of RiceTec's claims were withdrawn.
3. The Hoodia case ended without any benefit-sharing deal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The neem patent was revoked in 2000 and most Basmati claims were withdrawn; the Hoodia case ended in a benefit-sharing deal with the San people.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (biopiracy case – party) is correctly matched?
new.x: The neem patent was held by W.R. Grace; Basmati involved RiceTec, turmeric was challenged by CSIR and Hoodia concerns the San people.

new.s: The Traditional Knowledge Digital Library (TKDL) was set up in:
new.x: TKDL was set up in 2001 by CSIR and AYUSH to provide prior art.

new.s: India records about 811 crops and about how many crop wild relatives?
new.x: India has 811 crops and 902 crop wild relatives.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (Andhra Pradesh species – habitat) is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Slender loris – Dry Eastern Ghats scrub
new.x: Jerdon's courser lives in sparse scrub forest with bare ground, not mangroves.

new.s: Jerdon's courser inhabits:
o: Sparse scrub forest with bare ground
new.x: The Critically Endangered Jerdon's courser lives in sparse scrub forest with bare ground.

new.s: Sri Lankamalleswara Wildlife Sanctuary, declared for Jerdon's courser, is in which district?
new.x: Sri Lankamalleswara WLS is in Kadapa; Sri Penusila Narasimha WLS is in Nellore.

new.s: Jerdon's courser was rediscovered in:
new.x: Jerdon's courser was rediscovered in 1986.

new.s: The grey slender loris of Andhra Pradesh lives mainly in:
new.x: The slender loris lives in dry Eastern Ghats scrub, for example in Sri Venkateswara National Park.

new.s: Mahendra Girulu in the Eastern Ghats lies in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
new.x: Mahendra Girulu is in Srikakulam, not Anantapur.

new.s: The Andhra Pradesh State Biodiversity Board passes what share of Red Sanders profits to farmers?
new.x: APSBB gives 5% of Red Sanders profits to farmers; 45% is Red Sanders' share of NBA's ABS money.

new.s: About how many Biodiversity Management Committees has the Andhra Pradesh State Biodiversity Board set up?
new.x: APSBB works through about 13,000 BMCs and their PBRs.

new.s: Andhra Pradesh has India's ____ largest mangrove ecosystem.
new.x: AP has the second-largest mangrove ecosystem in India.

new.s: Norman Myers' hotspot concept was adopted by Conservation International in:
new.x: Myers proposed it in 1988 and CI adopted it in 1989.

new.s: The 1,500 endemic vascular plant threshold for a hotspot is over what share of the world total?
new.x: 1,500 endemic vascular plants equal over 0.5% of the world total.

new.s: When numerical thresholds were set in 1999, how many hotspots were recognised?
new.x: There were 25 hotspots in 1999; the count rose to 34, 35 and then 36.

new.s: How many 'hottest hotspots' with the highest endemism under the greatest threat are recognised?
new.x: There are 8 hottest hotspots, including Western Ghats-Sri Lanka.

new.s: Biodiversity hotspots hold about what share of the world's vertebrates as endemics?
new.x: Hotspots hold about 42% of vertebrates and 50% of vascular plants as endemics.

new.s: Biodiversity hotspots once covered about what share of Earth's land?
new.x: Hotspots once covered 15.7% of land; after about 86% habitat loss they cover only about 2.5%.

new.s: The global standard for Key Biodiversity Areas (2016) is led by:
new.x: KBAs are identified by an IUCN-led partnership; Global 200 is WWF's and hotspots are CI's.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (concept – body) is correctly matched?
new.x: Hotspots are a Conservation International concept; KBAs are IUCN-led and Global 200 is WWF's.

new.s: In India, the Andaman Islands fall within which biodiversity hotspot?
new.x: The Andamans belong to Indo-Burma; only the Nicobar Islands belong to Sundaland.

new.s: Which of the following Indian regions is NOT part of a global biodiversity hotspot?
new.x: The Vindhyas, like the Aravallis and Satpuras, are not a hotspot.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about biodiversity hotspots in India:
1. The Sundarbans are part of a global biodiversity hotspot.
2. The Nicobar Islands are part of the Sundaland hotspot.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The Nicobar Islands are India's only part of Sundaland; the Sundarbans are not a hotspot.

new.s: Indo-Burma hotspot in India covers the North-East south of the Brahmaputra and the:
new.x: Indo-Burma covers the North-East south of the Brahmaputra and the Andamans; it does not cover western India.

new.s: Besides invasive species, which event is a noted threat to the Nicobar part of the Sundaland hotspot?
new.x: Invasives and the 2004 tsunami threaten Sundaland/Nicobar; jhum is an Indo-Burma threat.

new.s: Young, fragile geology and landslides are major threats in which hotspot?
new.x: The Himalaya hotspot is threatened by young fragile geology, landslides and infrastructure.

new.s: The Kasturirangan High-Level Working Group limited the Western Ghats Ecologically Sensitive Area to about:
new.x: Kasturirangan limited the ESA to about 37% (about 60,000 sq km); Gadgil proposed the whole Ghats.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Western Ghats panels:
1. The Gadgil panel (WGEEP) was set up by MoEF in 2010.
2. The Kasturirangan group recommended the whole Western Ghats as an ESA.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Gadgil's WGEEP (2010) proposed the whole Ghats as ESA; Kasturirangan limited it to about 37%.

new.s: The Western Ghats UNESCO serial World Heritage Site has 39 component areas in how many clusters?
new.x: The 2012 serial site has 39 component areas in 7 clusters.

new.s: The IUCN 2025 World Heritage Outlook rated the Western Ghats as of:
new.x: The IUCN 2025 Outlook rated the Western Ghats 'significant concern'.

new.s: The Nicobar pigeon is an endemic species associated with which hotspot?
new.x: The Nicobar pigeon belongs to Sundaland; the hoolock gibbon belongs to Indo-Burma.

new.s: The Nilgiri tahr is endemic to the:
new.x: The Nilgiri tahr is a Western Ghats endemic, not a Himalayan species.

new.s: The Nilgiri marten and Malabar spiny dormouse are Western Ghats endemics found in:
new.x: Both are Western Ghats endemics of the Agasthyamalai area.

new.s: The Golden Mahseer (Tor putitora) is a:
new.x: Golden Mahseer is a fish of Himalayan streams.

new.s: Under the Biological Diversity Act, commercial use of bioresources by Indian entities is regulated by the:
new.x: SBBs regulate commercial use by Indian entities; the NBA handles foreign access and IPR.

new.s: The Biological Diversity Act, 2002 gives effect in India to the:
new.x: The Act implements the CBD of 1992.

new.s: In Union Territories, the State-level role under the Biological Diversity Act is performed by:
new.x: The State tier is SBBs, and in UTs, UT Biodiversity Councils.

new.s: The statutory National Biodiversity Authority Fund was created under the Biological Diversity Rules of:
new.x: The Biological Diversity Rules, 2024 followed the 2023 amendment and set up the NBA Fund.

new.s: Biodiversity Management Committees are key to achieving the objectives of which protocol?
new.x: BMCs are key to the Nagoya Protocol objectives and can levy collection fees.

new.s: About how many Biodiversity Management Committees existed in India in 2024?
new.x: There were about 2.62 lakh BMCs in 2024; about 2.72 lakh is the PBR count of June 2026.

new.s: Kasampatty Biodiversity Heritage Site is located in:
new.x: Kasampatty is in Tamil Nadu; Nallur is in Karnataka, Ameenpur in Telangana and Borjuli in Assam.

new.s: As of March 2026, India had how many Biodiversity Heritage Sites?
new.x: The NBA count was 54 in March 2026, up from 45 (2024) and 48 (2025).

new.s: Borjuli wetland Biodiversity Heritage Site, protecting wild rice, is in:
new.x: Borjuli wetland (Oryza rufipogon) is in Assam.

new.s: Jeevani, the anti-fatigue drug from Kani tribal knowledge, was developed by:
new.x: TBGRI developed Jeevani from the Kani tribe's knowledge of Arogyapacha.

new.s: Arogyapacha, the plant behind the Kani benefit-sharing model, is:
new.x: Arogyapacha is Trichopus zeylanicus.

new.s: In the IUCN Red List, 'NT' stands for:
new.x: NT means Near Threatened, not 'Not Threatened'.

new.s:
Arrange the following IUCN categories from highest to lowest risk of extinction:
1. Vulnerable
2. Critically Endangered
3. Near Threatened
4. Endangered
new.x: The order is CR, EN, VU, NT (then LC).

new.s: How many categories does the IUCN Red List have?
new.x: There are nine categories: EX, EW, CR, EN, VU, NT, LC, DD and NE.

new.s: In the Red Data Book, green pages denote species that are:
new.x: Green pages mark recovered species; red or pink pages mark endangered and critically endangered ones.

new.s: The IUCN was founded in:
new.x: IUCN was founded in 1948; the Red List began in 1964 and Green Status in 2021.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the IUCN?
o: Its headquarters is at Gland, Switzerland
Its Species Survival Commission runs specialist groups
new.x: IUCN is a union of governments and civil-society organisations, not a UN agency.

new.s: The Living Planet Index tracks vertebrate populations since:
new.x: WWF and ZSL's Living Planet Index tracks vertebrate populations since 1970.

new.s: The 2019 Global Assessment on Biodiversity was published by:
new.x: The Global Assessment is by IPBES, the 'Intergovernmental Panel on Nature', not WWF.

new.s: Of the 175,909 species assessed in IUCN Red List 2026-1, about how many are threatened?
new.x: 49,505 (about 28%) are threatened.

new.s: Co-extinction is listed as a cause of biodiversity loss in:
o: Both the Evil Quartet and HIPPO
new.x: Co-extinction belongs to the Evil Quartet; pollution and population belong only to HIPPO.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the HIPPO framework:
1. It was popularised by E.O. Wilson.
2. Its two 'P's stand for pollution and human population.
3. It includes co-extinction.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: HIPPO, popularised by Wilson, includes pollution and population; co-extinction is in the Evil Quartet.

new.s: Which species are examples of extinction caused by over-exploitation?
o: Steller's sea cow and passenger pigeon
Hawaiian crow and Père David's deer
new.x: Steller's sea cow and the passenger pigeon were lost to over-exploitation.

new.s: Which of the following activities restores ecological balance?
o: Removal of invasives with native restocking
new.x: Removing invasives with native restocking restores balance; the others disturb it.

new.s: Tropical rainforest cover has fallen from 14% to about what share of Earth's land surface?
new.x: Tropical rainforests fell from 14% to 6% of the land surface.

new.s: Habitat fragmentation hits which animals hardest?
new.x: Fragmentation disrupts movement and separates populations of migratory and wide-ranging mammals and birds.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about climate change as a driver of biodiversity loss:
1. Warming causes coral bleaching and ocean acidification.
2. A warming Arctic is opening up to alien plants.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Both are effects of climate change on biodiversity.

new.s: The fifth mass extinction, which ended the dinosaurs, occurred about:
new.x: The end-Cretaceous fifth mass extinction was about 66 million years ago.

new.s: How many mass extinctions occurred in the past 500 million years before the present one?
new.x: There were five past mass extinctions; the sixth is happening now.

new.s: Which of the following is classified as Extinct in the Wild?
new.x: The Hawaiian crow survives only in captivity; passenger pigeon and Steller's sea cow are Extinct; GIB is CR.

new.s: The IUCN Red List (2014) recorded how many extinctions in the last 500 years?
new.x: 784 extinctions in 500 years were recorded in 2014.

new.s: Lantana camara belongs to the family:
new.x: Lantana is in Verbenaceae, not Asteraceae.

new.s: Senna spectabilis, invasive in the Nilgiri-Bandipur-Wayanad landscape, is native to:
new.x: Senna spectabilis is from South America, not North America.

new.s: Which invasive species is called the 'Terror of Bengal'?
new.x: Water hyacinth, the worst aquatic weed, is called the Terror of Bengal.

new.s: Which invasive fish is banned in India?
new.x: The predatory African catfish (Clarias gariepinus) is banned in India.

new.s: Target 6 of the Kunming-Montreal GBF aims to cut the introduction of invasive alien species by at least ____ by 2030.
new.x: Target 6 seeks at least a 50% cut by 2030; 30% is the 30x30 figure of Target 3.

new.s: Which Kunming-Montreal GBF target aims to conserve 30% of land and sea by 2030?
new.x: Target 3 is 30x30; Target 6 deals with invasive alien species.

new.s: The new Schedule IV of the Wildlife (Protection) Act after the 2022 amendment lists:
new.x: Schedule IV lists CITES-appendix specimens; invasives are regulated under Section 62A.

new.s: The IUCN Red List status of the Asiatic lion is:
new.x: The Asiatic lion is Endangered, improved from Critically Endangered.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (species – IUCN status) is INCORRECTLY matched?
new.x: The leatherback turtle is Vulnerable, not Critically Endangered.

new.s: The Sangai deer is found in:
new.x: Sangai (EN) lives in Keibul Lamjao, Manipur.

new.s: The Great Indian Hornbill naturally inhabits:
o: Western Ghats and North-East hill forests
new.x: The Great Indian Hornbill lives in the Western Ghats and North-East hill forests.

new.s: Three new Critically Endangered plant species were reported in May 2026 from:
new.x: The three new CR plants came from AP's Eastern Ghats.

new.s: A 2026 survey of Western Ghats odonates recorded 143 species, of which how many are endemic?
new.x: 143 species were recorded, 40 of them endemic; only about 65% of recorded species were found.

new.s: Which species appears as a flagship, keystone and umbrella species?
new.x: The tiger is a flagship, keystone (apex predator) and umbrella species.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Jerdon's courser?
o: It occurs in Sri Lankamalleswara WLS, Kadapa
new.x: Jerdon's courser is not flightless.

new.s: The Gooty tarantula is listed under which Schedule of the Wildlife (Protection) Act?
new.x: It is in WPA Schedule II (Part G) and CITES Appendix II.
